response.title: Can I use a portable power station to recharge my RV's batteries when I'm camping without hookups?
response.answer:
Yes! You can use a portable power station to recharge your RV's house batteries while camping without hookups (boondocking). In fact, it's a practical way to extend your off-grid camping time.

There are several ways to do it, but the best method depends on your RV's electrical system and the portable power station you have.

3 ways to charge your RV batteries
Shop

1. Through your RV's shore power connection

Easiest method

Plug your RV's shore power cord into the power station's AC outlet, using the appropriate adapter.

Your RV's built-in converter will charge the house batteries, just as it would at a campground hookup.

Downside: Energy is lost converting DC to AC and back to DC.

Shop

2. Through a DC-to-DC battery charger

Potentially more efficient

Use a compatible DC-to-DC charger between the power station's DC output and your RV's house batteries.

This can avoid AC conversion losses, but requires compatible voltages, current limits, wiring and battery charging profiles.

Downside: More complicated, and not every power station supports it.

Shop

3. Recharge the power station with solar panels

Connect compatible solar panels to your portable power station, then use either of the methods above to recharge the RV batteries.

Advantage: You can replenish energy during the day without running a generator.

How much charge can you actually get?

Let's say you have a 1,000 Wh portable power station and a 12V RV house battery.

ILLUSTRATIVE ENERGY TRANSFER

Power station capacity

1,000 Wh

Energy reaching RV battery

~750–850 Wh

Assumes approximately 75–85% overall charging efficiency through an AC converter. Actual results vary.

That translates to roughly 55–65 Ah of charging at typical 12V battery charging voltages, before accounting for any RV appliances consuming power at the same time.

Important things to watch out for

Converter power draw: Your RV's converter may draw more power than a small power station can supply.

Other RV loads: Turn off high-draw appliances such as electric water heaters and air conditioners while charging.

Battery compatibility: Lead-acid, AGM and LiFePO4 batteries have different charging requirements.

Neutral-ground bonding: Some RV electrical systems may not work correctly with a power station's floating-neutral AC output. Use only manufacturer-approved solutions.

Avoid direct battery connections: Don't connect an unregulated 12V power station output directly to the battery terminals as a charging method.
